findings.title: Exact-model conditional relied on the top-level required list
findings.body: Round 1 flagged that the gemini-3.1-pro-high if/then clause could pass vacuously when auditor_tool is absent, since JSON Schema properties is vacuous for a missing key. The risk was not reachable: auditor_tool is in the schema's top-level required array. It was closed directly anyway by adding "required": ["auditor_tool"] to the then clause, making the conditional self-contained. Strict tightening; no proof that validated before changes verdict. Covered by tests/audit/test_agy_gemini31_model.py::test_exact_model_requires_auditor_tool_to_be_present. Round 2 Q1 and Q10(a): PASS.

findings.title: Round 1 was asked to verify the auditor report inside the tree it was auditing
findings.body: Producer prompt-scope defect, not a change defect. The canonical AUDITOR_REPORT.md is this audit's own output and cannot exist in the audited tree. The placement is forced: the trusted schema requires report_path under a single proof/ directory, while proof-only closure confines the successor commit to proof/pr_merge/embedded-audit/pr-1165/. Round 2 was given the ordering constraint and instructed to flag any file claiming the report already existed; it found none. Disclosed in the report itself. Round 2 Q6 and Q10(b): PASS.

findings.title: Claimed unauthorized addition of pal-mcp-clink to the auditor_tool enum
findings.body: Refuted. pal-mcp-clink is already present in the trusted schema on main at 5d694cc9898e5046b5da03319f20f48599c40ca8; this change does not touch the auditor_tool enum. The documentation line had omitted it and the diff corrects that omission, now stated explicitly in docs/ops/embedded-audit-proof.md so it cannot be misread. Round 1 saw only the diff, not main, so it could not distinguish documentation catch-up from an enum addition. Round 2, shown the full schema hunk, confirmed the enum is untouched. Round 2 Q10(c): PASS.
